name: Saronic
blurb: Autonomous surface vessels for the U.S. Navy and allied fleets, designed and built in Southeast Austin.
facts: Closed a $1.75B Series D at a $9.25B valuation in March 2026
Austin footprint is past 500,000 sq ft, anchored by its Eastside Commerce Center plant
Bought a shipyard in Franklin, Louisiana and is building a next-generation yard, Port Alpha

name: Firefly Aerospace
blurb: Alpha rockets, Blue Ghost lunar landers and Elytra orbital vehicles, designed in Cedar Park and test-fired at a ranch in Briggs.
facts: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed on the Moon in March 2025, the first fully successful commercial lunar landing
Listed on Nasdaq as FLY in August 2025
Cedar Park campus grew to 144,000 sq ft across three buildings in 2026

sites.label: Rocket Ranch: engine tests & rocket production

sources.label: KVUE: three new Cedar Park buildings

name: CesiumAstro
blurb: Active phased-array communication payloads for satellites, aircraft and munitions, and now whole satellites, starting with Element.
facts: Committing $500M to grow its Bee Cave HQ, including 270,000 sq ft of manufacturing space
Plans 550 new jobs, taking Central Texas headcount past 1,000 by 2030
Texas Space Commission grant of up to $10M for its Element satellite line

name: Allen Control Systems
blurb: Bullfrog, an AI-aimed robotic weapon station that turns a standard machine gun into a drone killer.
facts: Raised a $200M Series B at a $2.2B valuation in 2026
Bullfrog is fielded with the U.S. Army and Navy
Converting a 191,000 sq ft former office campus in North Austin into a factory

name: Aeon Industrial
blurb: Vertically integrated precision weapons: the Zeus tactical missile and ODIN autonomous targeting software.
facts: Founded in 2023; moved its HQ and manufacturing to Cedar Park in 2026
Expanding from 48,000 to 138,000 sq ft on Scottsdale Drive, down the street from Firefly
Flight-tested with Moog's turret under an Army Applications Laboratory contract

sources.label: The Real Deal: Cedar Park expansion

name: Perseus Defense
blurb: Guided micro-missiles for knocking down drones, from a Y Combinator team of NASA and Boeing alumni.
facts: Founded in 2025; picked Buda's Tower Business Park for its HQ
Plans roughly 400 jobs within five years

name: BAE Systems
blurb: Electronic warfare, sensors, autonomy and cyber systems, engineered and built in East Austin on the old Tracor campus.
facts: Descends from Tracor, founded in Austin in 1955, the city's first homegrown defense giant
Opened a $150M, 390,000 sq ft engineering and production facility in Austin

name: SpaceX · Starlink
blurb: SpaceX's Bastrop factory builds Starlink user terminals and is adding advanced semiconductor packaging.
facts: Roughly 700,000 sq ft today, with a 1M sq ft expansion planned
A $280M packaging R&D expansion backed by a $17.3M Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund grant

sources.label: Office of the Texas Governor: TSIF grant

name: Skyways
blurb: Long-range autonomous VTOL cargo aircraft for military logistics, like ship-to-ship resupply at sea.
facts: $37M U.S. Air Force AFWERX contract to scale production (2025)
Standing up a 250,000 sq ft production site in Tech Ridge

name: Nanohmics
blurb: Contract R&D in optics, advanced materials and sensing, much of it through Department of Defense SBIR programs.
facts: Founded in 2002 by three research scientists
A long-running SBIR performer for DoD and NASA

name: U.S. Army T2COM
blurb: The Army's Transformation and Training Command, formed in 2025 by merging Army Futures Command with TRADOC, runs from the UT System building downtown.
facts: Army Futures Command set up here in 2018, in an office tower rather than on a base
T2COM activated on Oct. 2, 2025 as a four-star headquarters
The Army kept the HQ in Austin for its innovation culture and the Army Software Factory

name: Army Software Factory
blurb: Active-duty soldiers spend three-year tours here as developers, designers, product managers and platform engineers.
facts: Based at Austin Community College's Rio Grande campus since 2021
A 10-year, $16M agreement with ACC was signed in January 2026; a Marine Software Factory followed

name: Army Applications Laboratory
blurb: The Army's startup-facing team, working out of Capital Factory to get commercial technology in front of soldiers fast.
facts: Stood up in 2018 alongside Army Futures Command
Its contracts helped fund flight tests like Aeon Industrial's missile-and-turret pairing

name: Applied Research Laboratories
blurb: ARL:UT, a University Affiliated Research Center working on acoustics, sonar, radar, communications and space geodesy for the Navy and DoD.
facts: Developed the high-resolution sonar installed on U.S. Navy submarines
One of 15 Department of Defense University Affiliated Research Centers

name: UT Center for Space Research
blurb: Orbit determination and space geodesy research; UT led the science for NASA's GRACE gravity-mapping satellites.
facts: Principal-investigator home of NASA's GRACE mission

name: Samsung Semiconductor
blurb: Samsung's U.S. foundry: two fabs on Parmer Lane and a new leading-edge fab in Taylor.
facts: Broke ground in March 1996 with the Longhorn Band and a rodeo; the $1.4B was then Texas' largest foreign investment
More than $18B invested in the two Austin fabs
Taylor: $37B+ planned, a $4.745B CHIPS Act award, and Tesla AI-chip production starting in 2026

name: NXP Semiconductors
blurb: Motorola's Austin chip business, spun out as Freescale in 2004 and bought by NXP in 2015. Two 200mm fabs still run here.
facts: Motorola came to Austin in 1974, the seed of the city's chip industry
About 2,700 employees across the Oak Hill and Ed Bluestein campuses
Has put its 155-acre Oak Hill campus, long its U.S. HQ, on the market

sources.label: KXAN: Oak Hill campus for sale

name: Applied Materials
blurb: Builds the deposition and etch systems that fabs worldwide run on, at a campus off U.S. 290 near Walter E. Long Lake.
facts: One of the largest manufacturing plants in the region
Also runs R&D, IT and data-center operations on Spectrum Drive in Northwest Austin

name: AMD
blurb: AMD's Austin campus designs processors and accelerators in the Southwest Parkway tech corridor.
facts: Part of the Lantana corridor alongside NXP's Oak Hill campus

name: SkyWater · Fab 25
blurb: A U.S.-only pure-play foundry making 130–65 nm chips for industrial, automotive and defense customers.
facts: Bought Fab 25 from Infineon in June 2025 for about $93M
Adds about 400,000 wafer starts a year and roughly 1,000 employees
Fab 25 was Spansion's main fab before Cypress and Infineon owned it

name: Silicon Labs
blurb: Low-power wireless chips (Bluetooth, Zigbee, Thread, Wi-Fi) for connected devices. Founded in Austin in 1996.
facts: Texas Instruments agreed to acquire it for about $7.5B in February 2026; closing expected in 2027

sources.label: TI: agreement to acquire Silicon Labs

name: Cirrus Logic
blurb: Low-power audio and mixed-signal chips that ship in hundreds of millions of phones and laptops, designed at its downtown HQ.
facts: Headquartered on West 6th Street in downtown Austin

name: Ambiq
blurb: Microcontrollers built on subthreshold-voltage circuits so wearables and sensors can run AI on tiny batteries.
facts: IPO on the NYSE as AMBQ in July 2025
Its chips are in more than 280 million devices

name: Mythic
blurb: Analog compute-in-memory processors that run AI inference inside flash memory cells at a fraction of GPU power.
facts: Raised $125M in December 2025
Acquired German AI-processor maker Videantis in January 2026

name: Neurophos
blurb: Optical processing units that do AI matrix math with light, using metamaterial modulators far smaller than conventional photonics.
facts: $110M Series A led by Gates Frontier in January 2026
Expanding its Domain HQ and opening a San Francisco engineering site

name: Canon Nanotechnologies
blurb: Develops nanoimprint lithography, stamping chip patterns into resist instead of projecting them with light.
facts: Started in 2001 as Molecular Imprints; acquired by Canon in 2014

name: Ideal Power
blurb: Bidirectional bipolar power semiconductors (B-TRAN) for EV contactors, solid-state breakers and grid gear.
facts: Listed on Nasdaq as IPWR

name: NI (Emerson)
blurb: The instruments and LabVIEW software used to test rocket engines, chips and radars. Founded in Austin in 1976.
facts: Acquired by Emerson in 2023; now Emerson's Test & Measurement business

name: Texas Institute for Electronics
blurb: A UT-led foundry for 3D heterogeneous integration, stacking chips made of different materials, for defense and industry.
facts: $1.4B: $840M from DARPA's NGMM program plus $552M from Texas
Refitting the original SEMATECH fab on Montopolis Drive
Tools slated to be in place in early 2026

name: Texas Advanced Computing Center
blurb: Runs some of the most powerful academic supercomputers in the U.S., now including NSF's Horizon.
facts: Horizon anchors NSF's Leadership-Class Computing Facility, with about 4,000 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs in phase one
Early users came onto Horizon in late summer 2026

name: Tesla · Giga Texas
blurb: Tesla's global headquarters and largest U.S. factory, on the Colorado River east of the airport.
facts: About 2,500 acres, with more than 10M sq ft of factory floor
Builds Model Y and Cybertruck and 4680 cells, and houses the Cortex AI training clusters
Tesla moved its HQ here in 2021; production began in 2022

name: Base Power
blurb: Installs large home batteries that keep houses running through outages and act as a virtual power plant for the grid, and builds them in Austin.
facts: $1B Series D at a $13B valuation in August 2026; more than $2.5B raised
Factory 1 is the old Austin American-Statesman printing plant, beside the bat bridge
Factory 2: a $265M, 486,000 sq ft plant near the airport

name: Aalo Atomics
blurb: Sodium-cooled modular reactors designed to be mass-produced in a factory and paired with data centers.
facts: $100M Series B in August 2025; more than $136M raised
Broke ground on its Aalo-X reactor at Idaho National Laboratory under DOE's Reactor Pilot Program
Opened a 40,000 sq ft reactor factory HQ off East Ben White in 2025

name: Last Energy
blurb: Small pressurized-water reactors (PWR-5) built like products rather than projects, for data centers and industry.
facts: Raised a $100M+ Series C in December 2025
Building a pilot PWR-5 at Texas A&M-RELLIS in DOE's reactor pilot program
Moved its headquarters from Washington, D.C. to Austin

name: Hyliion
blurb: Fuel-agnostic linear generators, largely 3D-printed, for data centers, defense and prime power.
facts: $41.7M U.S. Navy contract for megawatt-scale KARNO systems (July 2026)
The KARNO technology was acquired from GE Aerospace

name: Infinitum
blurb: Axial-flux motors with printed-circuit-board stators: lighter, quieter and more efficient than iron-core motors.
facts: Raised a $185M round in 2024 to scale production
Engineering HQ in Round Rock; motor plants in Mexico

sites.label: HQ & engineering
sites.address: 106 E Old Settlers Blvd, Round Rock

name: EnergyX
blurb: Membrane and sorbent technology that pulls lithium out of brine, developed in Austin labs and pilot plants.
facts: Opened a 40,000 sq ft Lithium Innovation HQ in Austin in 2024
Eni invested $225M for a stake in its Project Black Giant in Chile (July 2026)

name: Apptronik
blurb: General-purpose humanoid robots for factories and logistics, spun out of UT Austin's Human Centered Robotics Lab.
facts: Series A passed $935M with a $520M extension in February 2026, at a $5B+ valuation
Backers include Google, Mercedes-Benz, B Capital, John Deere and QIA
Leasing a 59,000 sq ft production warehouse across the street from its HQ

name: ICON
blurb: Robotic construction printers that print houses from concrete, plus lunar construction R&D for NASA.
facts: $57.2M NASA contract (2022) for Project Olympus lunar construction
Raised a $56M Series C in February 2025

name: The Boring Company
blurb: Designs and builds Prufrock tunnel boring machines and runs its global TBM operations center from Bastrop.
facts: Moved HQ and engineering to Bastrop by 2023
Opened a Global Operations Control Center there in 2025

name: Diligent Robotics
blurb: Moxi, a mobile manipulator that fetches supplies and runs errands for hospital nurses.
facts: Moxi works in health systems including Cedars-Sinai and Texas Medical Center

name: Fox Robotics
blurb: FoxBot autonomous forklifts that load and unload trailers at warehouse docks.
facts: Founded in Austin in 2017; acquired by Symbotic in February 2026
